title: The Robot Who Wanted a Name
summary: A family's new helper robot is just called Unit 7 until the youngest child insists it deserves a real name, and picking one together based on its quirks makes it feel like part of the family.
poll: A name can make something feel like part of a family.

versions.title: The Robot Who Wanted a Name
versions.text:
A big box came. It was for Lama. Inside was a new robot.

Its tag said Unit 7. That was all.

The robot did jobs. It washed cups. It swept the floor. It folded clothes.

It had fun habits too. It made a soft hum. It did this after each job. It set shoes in a neat row.

One night, Lama had an idea. "Unit 7 is not a name," she said. "It is just a number!" Her big brother sat up.

At the table, they all talked. They talked about its jobs. They talked about its hum.

Mom said the hum was like wind. Dad gave a smile. They found a new name. It was Breezy!

Breezy made a glad hum. The home felt full. It was like five, not four.

versions.title: The Robot Who Wanted a Name
versions.text:
Picture opening a big box and finding a new robot that looks back at you, with only a cold number for a name. That is just what happened at Lama's home one day, when Mom's new helper robot showed up.

The robot's tag said only "Unit 7," yet it proved very useful fast. It washed the cups after meals, swept the floor each morning, and folded the clean clothes into neat piles.

Beyond its jobs, Unit 7 had fun quirks that made it feel less like a plain machine. It hummed a soft tune after each job, and it set every pair of shoes in a neat row by the door. These small habits became part of its daily routine, and they slowly showed a kind of personality that felt warm for a machine.

One night, Lama had a new idea. "Unit 7 is not a name," she said firmly at the table. "It's just a number, but everyone in our home has a real name!" Her big brother, Faisal, looked up with interest, since he had not thought about it that way before.

That night, the family talked about a true name for their helper. They thought about its small jobs and its soft, happy hum. Faisal suggested a name based on the shoes, and Mom suggested one based on the hum, but no name felt quite right yet.

Mom said the hum was just like the wind blowing through a window on a cool night. Dad gave a warm smile, and then the family found a new name: Breezy!

From then on, Breezy hummed a big, glad tune while it worked. The home felt warm and full, almost as if it now held a family of five. By then, the family had come to appreciate Unit 7's small jobs and sweet quirks even more.

versions.title: The Robot Who Wanted a Name
versions.text:
Picture a large box being opened to show a brand-new robot gazing back, its only name a string of digits rather than something that felt genuinely real. That is exactly what happened at Lama's house one afternoon, when the helper robot her mother had ordered to ease a busy schedule finally arrived at the front door, still wrapped carefully in plastic.

The robot's tag read only "Unit 7," yet it swiftly proved itself remarkably useful around the house. It washed the dishes after dinner, swept the kitchen floor each morning, and folded the laundry into piles considerably neater than anyone else in the house ever managed.

Beyond its chores, Unit 7 displayed endearing little traits that made it feel like more than a plain machine. It hummed a cheerful tune whenever it finished a task, and it consistently arranged the shoes by the door into a neat row, sorted meticulously by size.

At first, Faisal barely noticed these details, since he usually remained absorbed in his own homework each afternoon. One evening, however, his younger sister Lama voiced an idea that startled everyone seated at the table. "Unit 7 is not a real name," she said firmly. "It's just a number, yet everyone in our family possesses a genuine name, so our robot deserves one too."

Faisal glanced up with sudden, genuine interest, realizing he had never previously considered the robot's identity in that particular light. That night, the family deliberated over what new name might suit their helper, weighing its everyday chores against its cheerful hum and its evident fondness for neat, orderly rows.

Their mother observed that the hum sounded remarkably like a gentle breeze drifting through an open window on a cool evening. Their father smiled warmly at the comparison, and the family soon reached a unanimous decision on a fitting name: Breezy.

From that moment onward, Breezy hummed an especially joyful tune while working busily throughout the house. The home instantly felt more complete, almost as though it now contained a genuine family of five rather than merely four, and Lama would often remark afterward that a true name had simply been waiting all along to be discovered.

versions.title: The Robot Who Wanted a Name
versions.text:
Picture the moment a large cardboard box is pried open to reveal a brand-new robot gazing back, its entire identity reduced to an impersonal string of digits rather than anything resembling a genuine, memorable name. That is precisely what unfolded at Lama's house one ordinary afternoon, when the long-awaited helper robot that her mother had ordered, hoping to ease an increasingly demanding schedule, finally arrived at their front door, still wrapped carefully in protective plastic and smelling faintly of new machinery and crisp cardboard.

The robot's name tag read only "Unit 7," and yet it swiftly proved itself remarkably useful throughout the household, far beyond what anyone, even her famously practical mother, had initially expected of so compact a machine. It washed the dishes after every dinner, swept the kitchen floor each morning without ever being asked, and folded the family's laundry into tidy piles considerably neater than anyone else in the household had ever managed to produce.

Beyond its assigned chores, however, Unit 7 displayed a handful of endearing little traits that made it feel like something considerably more than an ordinary machine built merely to perform tasks on command. It hummed a cheerful tune whenever it completed a task, and it consistently arranged every pair of shoes by the door into a perfectly neat row, sorted meticulously by size from smallest to largest, without ever being instructed to do so.

At first, Faisal scarcely registered these small details, since he usually remained thoroughly absorbed in his own homework each afternoon after school. One evening, however, his younger sister Lama voiced an idea that genuinely startled everyone seated around the table. "Unit 7 is not a real name," she declared firmly, setting down her fork with surprising conviction. "It's merely a number, yet everyone in our family possesses a genuine name, so surely our robot deserves one as well."

Faisal glanced up with sudden, genuine interest, recognizing that he had never previously considered the robot's identity in quite that particular light before. Lama had long believed, in her own quiet way, that names carried a subtle kind of power, granting whoever held one an unmistakable place within a family, and she felt certain that Unit 7 deserved exactly that sort of belonging.

That night, the family deliberated carefully over what new name might truly suit their helper, weighing its everyday chores alongside its cheerful hum and its evident fondness for neat, orderly rows of shoes. Their mother observed that the robot's hum sounded remarkably like a gentle breeze drifting through an open window on a cool evening. Their father smiled warmly at the comparison, and after several more suggestions were considered and gently set aside, the family reached a unanimous decision on a fitting new name: Breezy.

From that moment onward, Breezy hummed an especially joyful tune while working busily throughout the house, seemingly with renewed energy that had not been there before. The home instantly felt more complete and welcoming, almost as though it now contained a genuine family of five rather than merely four, and Lama would often remark afterward that a true name had simply been waiting all along, patiently, to be discovered. In many ways, she thought, a thoughtfully chosen name revealed as much about the people doing the choosing as it did about whichever creature, or machine, eventually came to wear it.

versions.title: The Robot Who Wanted a Name
versions.text:
When a helper robot bearing only the designation "Unit 7" arrived at Lama's household one ordinary afternoon, having been ordered by her mother to ease an increasingly demanding domestic schedule, nothing about its sterile, impersonal label suggested the subtle traits that would soon make it feel like an irreplaceable member of the family rather than a mere appliance performing programmed tasks. The robot proved immediately useful, washing dishes after dinner, sweeping floors each morning unprompted, and folding laundry into piles considerably neater than any human member of the household had ever managed, yet its usefulness alone was not what ultimately endeared it to the family that had welcomed it.

What distinguished Unit 7, in fact, were its small, idiosyncratic traits: a cheerful hum that accompanied the completion of every task, and an unwavering habit of arranging shoes by the door into a meticulously ordered row, sorted by size without ever being instructed to do so. These quirks, trivial though they might have seemed to an outside observer unfamiliar with the household, convinced Lama, the youngest member of the family, that a designation consisting merely of a letter and a digit could never adequately capture the robot's evident personality. "Unit 7 is not a real name," she insisted firmly at dinner one evening, pointing out that every other member of the family possessed a genuine name, and that fairness alone demanded the same consideration for their mechanical companion.

Her brother Faisal, initially skeptical of what he privately considered a rather sentimental notion, found himself reconsidering the robot's identity once he paused to notice the very traits his sister had already recognized. Various suggestions were floated before the family settled on its eventual choice: Faisal proposed naming the robot after its tidy habit with shoes, while their father briefly suggested something referencing its diligent work ethic, yet neither proposal captured the robot's personality quite as precisely as the sound that had first caught everyone's attention at the dinner table.

That evening, the family deliberated at considerable length, weighing the robot's daily chores against its endearing hum, which their mother likened to a gentle breeze drifting through an open window on a cool evening, until they eventually reached a unanimous decision: the robot would henceforth be called Breezy.

From that moment forward, Breezy appeared to hum with renewed enthusiasm while completing its daily chores, and the household itself seemed subtly transformed, as though the simple act of bestowing a genuine name had completed a family that had, until then, unknowingly lacked its fifth member. Lama would later reflect that the episode had taught her something she had not fully appreciated before: that the names people choose for others, whether human, animal, or machine, often reveal as much about the chooser's capacity for attentiveness and affection as they do about whoever eventually comes to wear them.

versions.title: The Robot Who Wanted a Name
versions.text:
When a helper robot bearing only the clinical designation "Unit 7" arrived at Lama's household one otherwise ordinary afternoon, having been ordered by her mother specifically to ease an increasingly demanding domestic schedule, nothing about its sterile, impersonal label hinted at the subtle idiosyncrasies that would, within a matter of weeks, transform it from a mere appliance performing programmed tasks into what felt like an irreplaceable member of the family. The robot proved immediately and unambiguously useful, washing dishes after every dinner, sweeping floors each morning entirely unprompted, and folding laundry into piles considerably neater than any human member of the household had ever consistently managed, yet its practical usefulness alone was not, in the end, what ultimately endeared it to the family that had so recently welcomed it into their home.

What distinguished Unit 7, rather, were its small, idiosyncratic traits, seemingly trivial on their own yet collectively significant: a cheerful hum that invariably accompanied the completion of every task, and an unwavering habit of arranging shoes by the door into a meticulously ordered row, sorted by size without ever having been explicitly instructed to do so. These quirks, however inconsequential they might have appeared to an outside observer unfamiliar with the household's daily rhythms, convinced Lama, the youngest and ostensibly least influential member of the family, that a designation consisting of nothing more than a single letter and a digit could never adequately capture so distinctive a personality. "Unit 7 is not a real name," she insisted firmly at dinner one evening, pointing out, with surprising conviction for someone so young, that every other member of the family possessed a genuine name, and that basic fairness therefore demanded equivalent consideration for their mechanical companion.

Her brother Faisal, initially skeptical of what he privately dismissed as a rather excessive sentimentality, found himself gradually reconsidering the robot's identity once he paused, almost reluctantly, to notice the very traits his sister had already recognized without hesitation. Various alternative names were proposed and subsequently discarded before the family settled on its eventual choice: Faisal suggested something referencing the robot's tidy habit with shoes, while their father briefly proposed a name connoting diligence, yet neither proposal captured the robot's personality quite as precisely as the simple sound that had first captured everyone's attention around the dinner table that evening.

The family deliberated at considerable length that night, weighing the robot's daily chores against its endearing hum, which their mother likened, rather poetically, to a gentle breeze drifting through an open window on a cool evening, until the discussion eventually yielded a unanimous decision: the robot would henceforth be known as Breezy, a name that managed, somehow, to feel both whimsical and entirely appropriate.

From that moment forward, Breezy appeared to hum with conspicuously renewed enthusiasm while completing its daily chores, and the household itself seemed subtly, almost imperceptibly transformed, as though the simple act of bestowing a genuine name had inadvertently completed a family that had, until then, unknowingly lacked its fifth member. Lama would later reflect that the entire episode had taught her something she had not previously and fully appreciated: that the names people choose to bestow upon others, whether human, animal, or machine, frequently reveal as much about the chooser's own capacity for attentiveness and affection as they ultimately do about whoever eventually comes to wear them.

keyWords.definition: a small, unusual habit or detail
keyWords.example: One quirk of our cat is that she only drinks water from a cup.

keyWords.definition: to offer an idea for someone to consider
keyWords.example: The coach suggested a new plan for practice.

keyWords.definition: to recognize the value of something and feel thankful for it
keyWords.example: We appreciated the extra help our neighbor gave us.

keyWords.definition: a regular set of actions done the same way each time
keyWords.example: Brushing my teeth every morning is part of my routine.

questions.stem: Which sentence best states the central idea of the article?
options: A family who gives their helper robot a real name because of its fun quirks
Unit 7 breaks down and the family must repair it with the help of a robot doctor and a neighbor
The family decides robots should never be given names, so they keep calling the robot Unit 7
Faisal teaches Unit 7 how to do new chores, such as washing the dishes and cleaning the floor
questions.why: The article follows Unit 7's chores and quirks, Lama's idea, and the family naming it Breezy.

wrong.B: Unit 7 never breaks down in the article.
wrong.C: The family decides the opposite: that Unit 7 deserves a name.
wrong.D: Faisal does not teach Unit 7 any chores.

questions.stem: According to the article, when does Unit 7 sweep the kitchen floor?
options: Only on weekends
Right before the family eats breakfast
Only after dinner
Each morning, without being asked
questions.why: The article says Unit 7 sweeps the floor each morning without being asked.

wrong.A: The article says mornings, not weekends only.
wrong.B: Breakfast time is not mentioned.
wrong.C: Sweeping happens in the morning, not after dinner.

questions.stem: What is unusual about the way Unit 7 arranges the shoes by the door?
options: It sorts them neatly by size without anyone asking
It hides them in a closet every night before bed
It arranges them by color, not by size, along the wall
It only lines up its own metal feet by the door
questions.why: The article says Unit 7 lines up the shoes neatly by size without being instructed to do so.

wrong.B: The shoes stay by the door, not in a closet.
wrong.C: The article says size, not color.
wrong.D: The shoes belong to the family, not the robot.

questions.stem: What caused Faisal to finally notice Unit 7's quirks?
options: Dad ordered him to pay attention to the robot at once
He read about robots in a book that he found at the library
Unit 7 stopped working completely and needed fixing right away
He finally paused to notice the traits Lama had already pointed out
questions.why: The article says Faisal glanced up with interest once he noticed the traits his sister had already recognized.

wrong.A: Dad never orders Faisal to pay attention.
wrong.B: No book about robots is mentioned.
wrong.C: Unit 7 never stops working.

questions.stem: In the article, the word quirk means —
options: a small unusual habit
a type of kitchen chore
a loud warning sound
a brand of robot
questions.why: The article uses quirk to describe Unit 7's humming and shoe-sorting habits, which are small, unusual details.

wrong.B: A quirk is not a chore itself.
wrong.C: A quirk is not a warning sound.
wrong.D: Quirk is not a brand name.

questions.stem: Why did the house feel 'more complete' after the robot was named Breezy?
options: Because Breezy stopped doing chores and just sat in the corner of the room
Because the family bought a second robot that was named Gust
Because naming Breezy made it feel like a true member of the family
Because the house became bigger after the robot was named
questions.why: Giving the robot a real name made the family feel like Breezy truly belonged, like a fifth family member.

wrong.A: Breezy keeps doing its chores after being named.
wrong.B: No second robot is mentioned.
wrong.D: The size of the house never changes.

questions.stem: How did Lama's reaction to Unit 7's quirks differ from Faisal's at first?
options: Lama ignored the quirks, while Faisal noticed them right away
Both siblings completely ignored the new robot at first
Faisal wanted to return the robot, while Lama agreed
Lama cared about the quirks right away, but Faisal needed more time
questions.why: Lama is the one who first has the idea about naming Unit 7, while Faisal only notices the quirks later that evening.

wrong.A: It is Lama, not Faisal, who notices the quirks first.
wrong.B: Lama clearly cares about the robot's quirks.
wrong.C: No one in the article wants to return the robot.

questions.stem: What happened right after Unit 7 arrived at the house?
options: The family immediately gave it the name Breezy
It began doing chores like washing dishes and sweeping
Faisal took it apart to see how it worked
The family decided to keep calling it Unit 7 forever
questions.why: Right after arriving, the article shows Unit 7 getting to work on chores; the naming happens later that evening.

wrong.A: The name Breezy comes later, after a family discussion.
wrong.C: Faisal never takes the robot apart.
wrong.D: The family ends up giving the robot a new name, not keeping the old one.

MID.prompt: Explain how Unit 7 went from being just 'a number' to feeling like part of the family. Use at least two details from the article.
checklist: I explained how Unit 7 changed from a number to a name.
I used at least two details from the article.
I organized my ideas in a clear order.
MID.modelAnswer: At first, Unit 7 was only known by a number, even though it did helpful chores like washing dishes and sweeping the floor. Lama noticed that Unit 7 had its own personality, shown by its happy hum and its careful habit of sorting shoes by size. Because of these quirks, the family suggested names and finally chose Breezy, which made the robot feel like a true part of the family instead of just a machine.

keyWords.definition: a particular quality or characteristic that someone, or something, has
keyWords.example: Patience is one of my grandmother's best traits.

keyWords.definition: to think about and discuss something carefully before deciding
keyWords.example: The judges deliberated for an hour before choosing a winner.

keyWords.definition: agreed on by everyone, with no one disagreeing
keyWords.example: The class vote for class president was unanimous.

keyWords.definition: causing someone to feel affection or fondness
keyWords.example: His endearing habit of singing while he cooked made everyone smile.

keyWords.definition: who or what someone or something truly is
keyWords.example: The old photograph helped reveal the soldier's true identity.

questions.stem: Which statement best expresses the central idea of the article?
options: Unit 7 malfunctions badly and must be completely reprogrammed by Faisal
Robots should never be treated as part of a real family
A family's care for a robot's small traits leads them to give it a real name
The story argues that chores are more important than companionship
questions.why: The article centers on the family noticing Unit 7's endearing traits and deciding it deserves a true identity, not just a number.

wrong.A: Unit 7 never malfunctions in the article.
wrong.B: The family's actions suggest the opposite view.
wrong.D: The article values both the chores and the robot's personality.

questions.stem: According to the article, what convinced Lama that 'Unit 7' could not adequately describe the robot?
options: The robot refused to do its chores around the house and then hid in the garage
The robot asked to be renamed after it heard a name in a song on the radio
Her parents insisted on a new name because they did not like the old one
A designation of a letter and a digit could not capture its personality
questions.why: Lama insists that a mere letter and number cannot capture the robot's evident personality.

wrong.A: Unit 7 performs its chores reliably throughout the article.
wrong.B: The robot never speaks or asks for anything.
wrong.C: It is Lama, not her parents, who first raises the idea.

questions.stem: What specific traits of Unit 7 are described as endearing?
options: Its ability to speak several different languages at home
Its humming after each task and its careful sorting of shoes by size
Its habit of cooking elaborate meals for the whole family
Its tendency to break down frequently in the middle of the working day
questions.why: The article highlights Unit 7's cheerful hum and its meticulous shoe-sorting as its endearing traits.

wrong.A: The article never mentions Unit 7 speaking languages.
wrong.C: Unit 7 is never described cooking meals.
wrong.D: Unit 7 is reliable, not prone to breaking down.

questions.stem: In the article, the word unanimous describes a decision that —
options: took a very long time to reach
was changed again the next day
everyone in the group agreed upon
only one person made alone
questions.why: A unanimous decision is one every member of the group agrees on, as the family does when naming the robot.

wrong.A: Unanimous describes agreement, not how long a decision takes.
wrong.B: The article never says the family changes the name later.
wrong.D: Unanimous means everyone agreed, not just one person.

questions.stem: Why did Faisal's view of the robot change over the course of the evening?
options: Dad ordered him to agree with Lama about the robot
The robot stopped working correctly during the evening
He had never actually disagreed with Lama about it at all
He noticed the same traits his sister had already pointed out
questions.why: Faisal reconsiders the robot's identity once he pauses to notice the traits Lama had already recognized.

wrong.A: Dad never gives Faisal such an order.
wrong.B: The robot works reliably throughout the article.
wrong.C: Faisal initially pays little attention, which is a form of disagreement in effect.

questions.stem: What can readers infer about why the family felt the house was 'more complete' after naming the robot?
options: A name gave the robot a place of belonging within the family
The robot became physically larger after being named by the whole family
The family planned to buy a second robot for the kitchen soon
The chores were suddenly finished much faster once it had a name
questions.why: Giving Unit 7 a genuine name made it feel like a true, included member of the household rather than an appliance.

wrong.B: The robot's size never changes in the article.
wrong.C: No second robot is ever mentioned.
wrong.D: The article does not suggest chores were completed faster.

questions.stem: Which correctly orders these events?
options: The robot is named Breezy, then the family notices its quirks, then Unit 7 arrives
Unit 7 arrives, then the family notices its quirks, then the robot is named Breezy
The family notices quirks, then Breezy is named, then Unit 7 arrives
Unit 7 arrives, then Breezy is named, then the family notices quirks
questions.why: Unit 7 first arrives and performs chores, the family then notices its quirks, and only afterward do they choose the name Breezy.

wrong.A: The robot cannot be named before it even arrives.
wrong.C: The robot must arrive before anyone can notice its quirks.
wrong.D: The family notices the quirks before deciding on a name.

questions.stem: Why does the author describe Faisal's early skepticism before he changes his mind?
options: To show that not everyone agrees at first, which makes the final unanimous choice feel earned
To argue that older siblings should never be trusted with family decisions of any kind
To explain in detail why Faisal secretly dislikes robots in general and does not want one
To criticize Lama's idea as being completely unreasonable and also quite unfair to the others
questions.why: Showing Faisal's initial doubt, followed by his change of heart, makes the family's eventual unanimous choice feel earned rather than automatic.

wrong.B: The article does not criticize older siblings in general.
wrong.C: Faisal does not dislike robots; he simply had not noticed Unit 7's traits yet.
wrong.D: The article treats Lama's idea as reasonable, since the whole family comes to agree.

HIGH.prompt: The story suggests that giving something a thoughtful name can change how we feel about it. Do you agree or disagree? Support your position with at least two pieces of evidence from the article.
checklist: I supported my position with specific evidence from the article.
I addressed a point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I agree that giving something a thoughtful name can change how we feel about it. Before Unit 7 had a name, it was only seen as a useful machine, even though it had endearing traits like its cheerful hum and its meticulous shoe-sorting. Once the family deliberated and reached a unanimous decision to call it Breezy, the robot's identity shifted, and the home felt more complete, as though a true fifth family member had joined them. Someone might argue that a name cannot really change a machine, since Breezy still does the exact same chores as before, but the family's own feelings clearly changed, which shows that a name can matter even if the robot itself stays the same.

LOW.stem: Who said the hum was like wind?
options: Lama's dad
Lama's brother
Lama's mom
Lama herself
LOW.why: The text says Mom said the hum was like wind.

wrong.A: Dad only gave a smile.
wrong.B: Her brother sat up but did not compare the hum to wind.
wrong.D: Lama had the idea for a name, but Mom made the wind comparison.

LOW.stem: Why did the home feel like five, not four?
options: Breezy joined the family
A new guest came to stay
Lama's cousin moved in
Another robot came in a box
LOW.why: After the robot got a name, it felt like one more member of the family.

wrong.B: No guest comes in the story.
wrong.C: No cousin is in the story.
wrong.D: Only one robot arrives.

LOW.stem: In the story, the word neat means —
options: loud and fast
old and broken
dirty and wet
clean and tidy
LOW.why: Unit 7 set the shoes in a neat row, so the shoes were tidy and in order.

wrong.A: A row of shoes is not loud or fast.
wrong.B: The shoes were not broken.
wrong.C: Neat is the opposite of messy, so dirty is wrong.

LOW.stem: What did the family do after Lama shared her idea?
options: They sent the robot back
They talked about its jobs
They went to bed right away
They bought a new robot
LOW.why: After Lama's idea, they all talked at the table about its jobs and its hum.

wrong.A: They kept the robot and named it.
wrong.C: They stayed up and talked first.
wrong.D: They kept Unit 7 and did not buy another.

MID.stem: What did Mom say Unit 7's hum was like?
options: The wind blowing through a window
A bird singing early in the day
Rain falling on the roof
A soft song from the radio
MID.why: Mom said the hum was just like the wind blowing through a window on a cool night.

wrong.B: Mom did not mention a bird.
wrong.C: Mom did not mention rain.
wrong.D: Mom did not mention a radio.

MID.stem: In the article, the word appreciate means —
options: to forget about
to value highly
to carry away
to count again
MID.why: By the end, the family saw how good the robot's small jobs and sweet quirks were, so they valued them.

wrong.A: The family did not forget the robot.
wrong.C: Nobody carries the robot away.
wrong.D: Counting is not what the family does.

MID.stem: Why did Lama say Unit 7 needed a real name?
options: The tag was too long to read
Mom wanted a new robot
All the others had a name
The robot asked for a new name
MID.why: Lama said that Unit 7 was just a number but everyone in their home has a real name.

wrong.A: The tag was short, only "Unit 7."
wrong.B: Mom did not ask for a new robot.
wrong.D: The robot never speaks in the story.

MID.stem: What does the family's talk about the robot's jobs and hum show?
options: They wanted to sell the robot
They did not like the robot
They felt the robot was only a machine
They saw it as more than a machine
MID.why: They looked at its quirks and thought of a true name for it, as they would for a person.

wrong.A: Nothing says they want to sell the robot.
wrong.B: They came to appreciate it more.
wrong.C: Naming it shows they felt it was more than a tool.

HIGH.stem: Why had Lama's mother ordered the helper robot?
options: To ease a busy schedule at home
To give Faisal a new friend
To win a prize at school
To replace an old washing machine
HIGH.why: The text says the robot was ordered to ease a busy schedule.

wrong.B: A friend for Faisal is not mentioned as the reason.
wrong.C: Prizes are not mentioned.
wrong.D: No washing machine is mentioned.

HIGH.stem: In the article, the word meticulously most nearly means —
options: with great care
in a hurry
by pure luck
without any help
HIGH.why: Sorting shoes by size takes close attention, so meticulously means with great care.

wrong.B: Sorting by size is slow work, not hurried.
wrong.C: Sorting by size is on purpose, not luck.
wrong.D: The word is about care, not help.

HIGH.stem: How did the robot's folded laundry compare with the piles others made?
options: It was messier than before
It was neater than others'
It was about the same
It was too small to use
HIGH.why: The text says the robot folded laundry into piles considerably neater than anyone else managed.

wrong.A: The piles were neater, not messier.
wrong.C: The text says they were better than the family's.
wrong.D: Size of piles is not mentioned.

HIGH.stem: What does Lama's last remark suggest about the name Breezy?
options: It was chosen by a vote
It was a name from a book
It fit who the robot already was
It was picked by Faisal alone
HIGH.why: Lama says a true name had been waiting to be discovered, meaning it matched the robot's hum and personality.

wrong.A: The family decided together, but no vote is described.
wrong.B: No book is mentioned.
wrong.D: Their mother thought of the breeze comparison, not Faisal alone.
